db_evidence.notes: All 5 rollouts correctly located the right anchor event (ice-cream + taxi entry at ~176808-176838) and the right exit/crowd window (~176838-176928, i.e. video-14 local ~19560-19650) using semantic_search and run_sql — anchor localization was not the failure mode. However the textual memory tables (episodes/visual_clips/event_steps/topic_facts/semantic_triples) only describe the scene qualitatively ('dense crowd of fans holding up smartphones', 'a woman with long dark hair briefly leans into the frame') and never state a specific count; no row anywhere in the DB gives '5'. The count is only recoverable by close frame-by-frame visual inspection of the ~60-90s crowd scene, which is genuinely chaotic (dozens of overlapping fans, motion blur, occlusion, phones raised for filming vs. for a joint photo look identical for much of the footage). Manually reviewing frames t176838-t176893 confirms a dense multi-person crowd pressed against the open taxi door, consistent with more than the 1-2 people the clip_qa sub-agent isolated, but confidently enumerating exactly 5 distinct 'came up to take a photo with him' individuals (vs. crowd members merely filming from a few feet away) is itself a hard, borderline-subjective visual judgment call even on manual review.

root_causes: Systematic visual undercount: every clip_qa call, regardless of the exact window (30s vs 60s) or the calling rollout's SQL thoroughness, converged on 1-2 distinct photo-takers versus a reference of 5, indicating the clip_qa sub-agent's frame sampling in a dense, fast-moving mob scene consistently misses/merges distinct individuals rather than any one rollout making an isolated mistake.

No textual DB evidence anywhere states or implies a count of 5; the ambiguity between 'crowd filming from nearby' and 'came up to take a photo with him' is not resolvable from stored text and requires fine-grained visual tracking that none of the visual sub-agent calls performed (only a handful of frames were inspected per call).

None of the 5 rollouts tried a second clip_qa call with a different/longer window or asked the sub-agent to re-examine ambiguous crowd members after getting a low count, despite the question's phrasing ('how many') inviting a sanity check when the visual answer felt low relative to the described 'dense crowd'.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly identified the anchor event (ice-cream + taxi entry) and the correct post-exit time window via semantic_search/run_sql, so retrieval/localization of the right moment was accurate and consistent across rollouts.

The read_skill sequence (general-retrieval, locating-time-intervals, counting-and-ordering, semantic-search, sql-schema, visual-verification) correctly routed the agent from text search to a mandatory visual verification for a count that text couldn't resolve.
transferable_lessons: For 'how many people came up to X' counts inside a dense/chaotic crowd scene, a single clip_qa call sampling a handful of frames is insufficient and biased low; the agent should request multiple overlapping clip_qa calls (or a longer window with denser frame sampling) and explicitly ask the sub-agent to track each individual across consecutive frames rather than judge from 2-3 stills.

When the visual sub-agent's count feels low relative to a DB description like 'dense crowd of fans holding up smartphones' and 'photo-filled scene', treat that as a signal to re-verify with a wider or denser visual pass before submitting, rather than trusting the first clip_qa answer.

Counting questions with ambiguous inclusion criteria (posed selfie vs. filming from the crowd) benefit from having the sub-agent enumerate every candidate person with evidence (frame id + description) rather than returning only a final number, so the calling agent can sanity-check borderline cases itself.
open_questions: Whether the reference count of 5 was produced by a human/automatic annotator with access to the full uncompressed video (able to track individuals frame-by-frame) versus a looser definition of 'came to take photos' that counts more of the crowd than the models did — this could not be fully confirmed without a full manual frame-by-frame count of the entire 176838-176928 window.

Whether extending the clip_qa window slightly beyond 176898 (up to when he actually closes the car door, ~176928) would surface additional distinct approachers the rollouts missed by stopping at 176868/176898.
